The first public test version of **NetSketch**: plan, simulate and learn home networks. Draw your home, place real routers, mesh nodes and access points, see where the Wi-Fi reaches and why a cable is slow, then send packets through it all. Every problem it finds comes with a plain-English explanation and, where it can, a one-click fix.

NetSketch started as a modern successor to [Filius](https://www.lernsoftware-filius.de/), the classic tool for teaching how networks work. It keeps the teaching side and adds what you need to plan a real home or small office. It also opens old Filius projects (`.fls`).

> **Beta:** the planning and teaching features are complete, and 99 automated tests run on Linux, Windows and macOS. The Windows and macOS builds haven't been tried by hand yet. Please report anything odd under [Issues](https://github.com/NilsBriggen/netsketch/issues).

## Downloads

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `NetSketch-0.1.0-x64.msi` | **Windows 10/11**: installs NetSketch with a Start-menu entry, and `.netplan` files open in it |
| `NetSketch-0.1.0-x64-portable.exe` | Windows, without installing |
| `NetSketch-x86_64.AppImage` | **Linux** (x86-64, GTK 3): `chmod +x NetSketch-x86_64.AppImage`, then run it |
| `netsketch-macos-arm64.tar.gz` | **macOS** on Apple silicon: unpack and run `netsketch` |
| `NetSketch-Survey-0.1-beta.apk` | **Android 10+**: the companion app for measuring Wi-Fi on site |

The builds aren't code-signed:
- **Windows:** SmartScreen may say the publisher is unknown. Choose *More info → Run anyway*.
- **macOS:** if it refuses to open the app, run `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine netsketch` once.
- **Android:** allow installing apps from your browser or file manager when it asks.

## What's in it

**Plan a real home**
- Walls by material, several storeys with real heights, a floor-plan picture to trace over, outdoor areas, and cable routes drawn along the walls.
- A catalog of **287 real devices** from 25 brands, with every Swisscom router from Centro Grande to Internet-Box 5 Pro and the boxes of Sunrise, Salt and Quickline. It also has **56 Swiss internet plans** and **19 powerline kits**, and every entry links to the source of its specs.
- Ports that work like the real thing (10G SFP+, 2.5G, 1G, WAN), so each cable's speed comes from the ports at both ends. PoE budgets, LACP bundles, VLANs, guest Wi-Fi, firewall and parental-control schedules, UPnP, ad blocking, IPv6 with prefix delegation, VPN with a carrier-grade-NAT check, QoS, Wi-Fi 7 multi-link and UPS runtime are all included.
- A shopping list with prices, the length of cable to lay, yearly power use and cost, and a side-by-side comparison of two options.

**See the Wi-Fi**
- A coverage heat map per storey and band (2.4/5/6 GHz) from a multi-wall model: distance, each wall's material and angle, and floors.
- European channel rules, radar (DFS) channels, neighbours' interference, airtime, roaming and band steering. There's also a coverage score per storey and a suggestion for where another access point helps most.
- Calibrate the model with real measurements from the phone app.

**Simulate and learn**
- DHCP, DNS, NAT (including carrier-grade NAT on mobile lines), routing, RIP, VLANs, spanning tree, ARP and MAC tables, and mail that follows MX records.
- A terminal on every device (`ping`, `traceroute`, `ipconfig`, `nslookup`, `speedtest`, `wifi`, `stp` …) and a built-in browser.
- A packet log with a per-packet layer view (Ethernet, IP with TTL, TCP with sequence numbers), step-by-step packet mode, and "what if this breaks?".
- 19 lessons with a quiz each, 10 ready-made scenarios, and 5 "find the fault" exercises with *Check my work*.

**Comfort:** English and German; dark, light and high-contrast themes; adjustable text size; keyboard use of the map; undo/redo; autosave.

## NetSketch Survey (Android)

Link the phone to NetSketch on your computer (it finds it on your Wi-Fi; you enter a 4-digit code), tap where you stand on your floor plan and press *Measure here*: every network heard there lands in NetSketch, pinned in place. New in this version:

- A plain-language verdict for each spot: weak signal, a phone sticking to a far access point, the slow band, a crowded 2.4 GHz channel and which channel to try, a busy channel, open or WEP networks.
- A channel chart per band, like a Wi-Fi analyser, with your networks highlighted.
- A speed test that measures **upload** and delay variation too.
- A zoomable floor plan (pinch, drag, double-tap). Your points show in colour by signal strength; tap one to see what was measured there.
- Points can be renamed, measured again at the same spot, or deleted (with a confirmation).
- A live graph of the last minute's signal.
- It handles Android's limit of 4 Wi-Fi scans every 2 minutes: it waits with a countdown instead of reusing stale results.
- It follows the phone's language (English or German) and its dark or light setting.

Without a computer nearby it keeps the points and shares them as a file you import later. Setup steps are in [INSTALL.txt](https://github.com/NilsBriggen/netsketch/blob/v0.1-beta/companion-android/INSTALL.txt).

## Known limits
- The built-in browser shows simple pages only (no tables, lists or styles beyond the basics).
- Spanning tree treats a device that uses the old short cost scale as classic STP (slow convergence) rather than asking it.
- Catalog power draw, prices and launch years are partly estimates; each entry's note says which.
- macOS builds are for Apple silicon only.

NetSketch is free software under the **GPL-3.0**.
